hormuz_disruption.label: Iran / Hormuz Disruption
hormuz_disruption.last_note: Tankers are resuming transit and WTI briefly broke below 70 dollars today for the first time since March 2, indicating the market is pricing in easing disruption risk, but no formal reopening agreement exists and Iran has not rescinded its operational-area declaration.

stagflation_regime.label: Stagflation Regime
stagflation_regime.last_note: BLS confirmed May CPI at 4.2 percent YoY up from 3.8 percent in April, the FOMC held at 3.50 to 3.75 percent on June 17 with markets pricing a hike by October 2026, locking in the higher-for-longer stagflation regime with no policy escape valve visible.

ai_bubble_risk.label: AI Bubble Risk Q4 2026
ai_bubble_risk.last_note: Statista confirmed hyperscaler capex tracking toward 725 billion in 2026 with capital intensity at 45 to 57 percent of revenue, but big tech has already issued 100 billion in bonds this year and investors are demanding record CDS protection, raising the debt sustainability question into Q4.

gold_supercycle.label: Gold Supercycle
gold_supercycle.last_note: Gold at 4013 is now trading BELOW the 200-day moving average of approximately 4340 cited by JPMorgan, central bank net purchases collapsed to only 16 tons in Q1 2026, and the risk of an October Fed rate hike is an active headwind, making the supercycle narrative technically broken in the near term.

copper_deficit.label: Structural Copper Deficit
copper_deficit.last_note: Spot treatment charges at minus 70 dollars per ton confirm extreme structural tightness at the concentrate level and China smelters have cut output over 10 percent in 2026, but Goldman projects only a 160kt surplus-to-balance in 2026 and soft Chinese refined demand at minus 8 percent YoY caps the near-term bull case.

nuclear_renaissance.label: Nuclear Renaissance
nuclear_renaissance.last_note: AI data center power demand structural thesis remains intact with Goldman projecting 7.6 trillion in AI-related capex through 2031 and Microsoft disclosing an 80 billion backlog of Azure orders constrained purely by power availability, making nuclear baseload the only viable 24/7 solution at gigawatt scale.

ALAB.note: Core AI connectivity thesis is intact with Q1 2026 revenue up 93 percent YoY and Q2 consensus pointing to 150 percent growth, but the stock surged 70 percent in 30 days to a P/E of 94 and Northland downgraded to Market Perform citing valuation, meaning the thesis is valid but the entry price has become the primary risk.

POWL.note: Power infrastructure thesis tied to AI data center buildout remains structurally intact given the confirmed 80 billion Azure power backlog and 725 billion in 2026 hyperscaler capex, but at P/E 42.84 with negative FCF momentum the stock offers limited margin of safety if any capex pause materialises.

MOD.note: AI liquid cooling thesis is confirmed by Schneider Electric calling direct-to-chip liquid cooling foundational for high-density deployments in April 2026, but MOD carries negative FCF of minus 101 million and the thesis is being competed away by larger HVAC and data center cooling specialists.

GFS.note: GFS specialty node and design-win thesis remains directionally valid but the stock is priced as a commodity foundry at P/E 33 with no AI-pure-play premium, and the Hormuz easing removes the near-term reshoring urgency argument that was a secondary catalyst.

CRDO.note: FY2026 revenue of 1.34 billion up 206 percent with FY2027 guidance for over 80 percent growth and optical revenues exceeding 600 million validates the DustPhotonics silicon photonics acquisition thesis fully, and at a forward P/S of 14.98 versus ALAB at 20.26 CRDO offers the better valuation within the same connectivity trade.

ARM.note: ARM at P/E 116 remains severely overvalued and the in-house custom silicon acceleration by Google, Amazon, and Microsoft structurally erodes ARMs long-term royalty TAM even as near-term licensing revenue holds; thesis has not changed and the risk-reward remains deeply unfavourable.

S.note: SentinelOne cut 8 percent of its workforce and guided lackluster near-term revenue, signaling competitive displacement by Palo Alto Networks and CrowdStrike in the AI-native security platform race; the original high-growth autonomous SOC thesis has materially weakened and the stock has drifted from a growth story to a restructuring story.

ZS.note: Zscaler has the strongest FCF in cybersecurity at $1.1 billion but the AVOID signal reflects valuation compression risk at P/E of 26.98 as rising 10Y yields at 4.509 percent systematically reprice long-duration growth assets; FCF strength does not offset duration risk in the current macro regime.

AXON.note: AXON Q1 2026 revenue of 807 million up 34 percent with ARR at 1.5 billion confirms the public safety AI platform flywheel is intact, and the thesis has not drifted as AXON is not an Iran war or AI-capex play but a government SaaS compounder with visible multi-year contract revenue.

ISRG.note: Intuitive Surgical has zero debt, $4.5B cash, 23% revenue growth, and $2.3B FCF making it a genuine compounder, but at 36x forward earnings and 29.4% below highs the surgical robotics moat thesis is unchanged — the drift is purely valuation-related, not fundamental, and the stock remains a hold-not-add until the multiple contracts further.

RXRX.note: Recursion Pharmaceuticals has revenue growth of minus 56.1%, is burning $178M in FCF with negative operating margins of minus 1985%, and is 55.2% below its 52-week high — the original AI drug discovery thesis has collapsed as clinical pipeline progress has not justified the technology premium and this is now a capital destruction story with no near-term catalyst.

JEDI.note: The drone and modern warfare rearmament thesis is structurally intact given the Hormuz crisis has accelerated defense technology procurement, but at 25% below highs and with no fundamental data available for an ETF wrapper this remains a theme trade that requires a defined technical base before adding risk.

CWAN.note: Clearwater Analytics has 74.4% revenue growth and $160M FCF which is operationally compelling, but analyst targets of $24.47 to $24.55 against the current $24.35 price provide virtually zero upside consensus — at PEG of 10.24 and EV/EBITDA of 73.69 the institutional fintech thesis is fully priced with no margin of safety.

GRAB.note: Grab at $3.30 with $6.5B cash, 23.5% revenue growth, and PEG of 0.87 is the most asymmetric deep value setup in the portfolio on a pure fundamentals basis, but the stock is 50.2% below highs and the Southeast Asia super-app monetization thesis requires a specific catalyst such as a buyback announcement or profitability upgrade to unlock value — thesis intact, no trigger yet.

VRT.note: Vertiv is a direct beneficiary of the above 1 trillion dollar 2026 data center capex cycle with power constraint urgency confirmed by the Microsoft 80 billion dollar Azure backlog, but stretched valuation demands flawless execution at a time when macro uncertainty is high.

MU.note: MU led the chip stock rally on June 15 on Iran deal optimism and structural AI memory demand is intact given that memory cost inflation drove data center capex higher in Q1 2026, but the stock is cyclical and a stagflation-driven consumer slowdown could compress DRAM pricing outside the AI data center vertical.

AMD.note: AMD surged on June 15 following an analyst upgrade and the Iran deal catalyst, with the company announcing up to 2 billion pounds in UK AI investment and the MEXT memory optimization acquisition signaling a serious data center strategy, but the stock at 548.80 dollars trades at a premium that assumes continued hyperscaler GPU wallet share gains from Nvidia.
